claimLedger.claim: Physical problems after birth may relate to pregnancy, birth or caregiving loads; ask GP/health visitor anytime; postnatal check ~6–8 weeks is a good time to raise issues.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Your post-pregnancy body · not stated on fetched page

claimLedger.claim: Postnatal check 6–8 weeks after birth to confirm recovery; invite discussion of continence, perineal pain, mental health.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Your 6-week postnatal check · Page last reviewed 9 October 2026
claimLedger.limitations: UK pathway; local Indian timing may differ

claimLedger.claim: Baby blues usually within 2 weeks; seek help if low mood continues or you struggle; urgent help for thoughts of harm to self or baby.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Postnatal depression · Page last reviewed 18 March 2026
claimLedger.limitations: UK services listed; crisis pathways differ in India—use local emergency numbers

claimLedger.claim: Recovery takes time; strengthen abdominal and pelvic-floor muscles to help avoid leakage, heaviness and back/pelvic pain.
claimLedger.sourceSection: POGP · Exercise and Advice After Pregnancy · Publication date on catalogue page 29 Nov 2022
claimLedger.limitations: UK booklet; exercise examples still need individual screening

claimLedger.claim: Hormonal ligament effects can last 6 months or more postnatally; return to exercise should be gradual.
claimLedger.sourceSection: POGP · Advice & Guidance for Exercise in the Childbearing Years · not stated
